claims.text: The proposed intervention is sub-monolayer Pt deposition by ALD on La-doped CeO2-ZrO2 followed by an in situ stabilization treatment.
This intervention will enhance catalytic activity in automotive exhaust catalysis.
This intervention will improve catalyst durability under high-temperature redox cycling.
This intervention will reduce overall platinum consumption.
Pretreating La-doped CeO2-ZrO2 provides anchoring sites suitable for isolated Pt atoms.
ALD at sub-monolayer coverage generates atomically dispersed Pt on La-doped CeO2-ZrO2.
Low-temperature annealing or chemical grafting can lock isolated Pt atoms in place on this support.
The resulting Pt species will be uniformly anchored across the La-doped CeO2-ZrO2 support.
Isolated metal centers provide maximum atom efficiency.
Atomically dispersed Pt provides greater active-site exposure than Pt nanoparticles or agglomerates.
La-modified ceria-based supports have enhanced oxygen storage, oxygen mobility, reducibility, and resistance to sintering.
The oxygen-storage and redox properties of La-doped CeO2-ZrO2 further stabilize atomically dispersed Pt.
The additional stabilization treatment maintains atomic Pt dispersion during prolonged cycling at 600-800°C.
Maintaining atomic Pt dispersion increases catalytic turnover.
Maintaining atomic Pt dispersion reduces sintering and thereby improves durability.
The stabilized ALD catalyst will improve conversion efficiency by 10-20% relative to conventional impregnated Pt catalysts.
The stabilized ALD catalyst will exhibit less Pt agglomeration than conventional impregnated Pt catalysts.
Conventional impregnated Pt catalysts use higher Pt loadings than the proposed catalyst.
The expected benefits are contingent on redox cycling between 600°C and 800°C.
Insufficient stabilization or operation outside 600-800°C may diminish the performance gains.

contradictions.description: The predicted improvement is defined relative to a conventional impregnated Pt catalyst, but the falsification experiment compares stabilized ALD only with non-stabilized ALD. It therefore does not directly test the stated baseline-relative activity, durability, or Pt-consumption claims.
